sources.title: The Theory of Quantum Information (2018 pre-publication draft)
A computable measure of entanglement
sources.authors: G. Vidal and R. F. Werner
sources.type: primary paper; inspected author arXiv v1 dated 2001-02-22

assumptions: rho and sigma are density operators on the same finite-dimensional Hilbert space.
The displayed finite trace expression requires support(rho) contained in support(sigma); otherwise the relative entropy is +infinity. Zero eigenvalue terms use 0 log 0 = 0.
variables: rho, sigma: normalized positive semidefinite operators; log: operator logarithm on the relevant support.
patches.units: Dimensionless information: bits for base-2 logarithms (Watrous convention); nats for natural logarithms. Use one base consistently; S here has no k_B factor.
patches.regime: Not a symmetric metric. The source defines the support extension explicitly; no commutativity assumption is needed.

patches.regime: Directed quantity -S(A|B), which can be negative. For channel interpretation A purifies the channel input and B is its output. This single-state quantity is not by itself the regularized quantum capacity. Source X maps to A and Y to B; tensor reordering leaves entropy unchanged.

assumptions: rho is a normalized density operator on a finite-dimensional bipartite Hilbert space; T_B is transposition on B in a fixed local orthonormal basis.
variables: ||X||_1: trace norm, Tr sqrt(X dagger X); T_B: partial transpose, not physical time reversal.
patches.regime: Nonnegative and zero for PPT states, including possible PPT-entangled states; zero does not establish separability in general. Source transposes A instead: rho^(T_B)=(rho^(T_A))^T, and full transposition preserves singular values, so both choices give the same norm.

sourceLocations.locator: Sec. I, Eq. (1), p. 1; partial-transpose definition Sec. II, Eq. (3), p. 2. Author arXiv v1 (22 February 2001), not a claimed inspection of the 2002 journal typesetting.

patches.theoryRelationship: Definition checked in the authors’ arXiv manuscript; the A/B partial-transpose convention conversion is explicit. Prior source links remain provenance.

assumptions: rho is a normalized finite-dimensional bipartite density operator; partial transposition uses a fixed local basis.
variables: ||X||_1: trace norm; T_B: transpose on B; log_2: base-two logarithm.
patches.regime: Equals log_2(2 N + 1); vanishes for every PPT state and therefore does not detect all entanglement. Source T_A converts to T_B by full transposition, which preserves the trace norm. No claim of convexity is made.

sourceLocations.locator: Sec. I, Eq. (2), p. 1; Eq. (1) for the negativity relation; author arXiv v1 (22 February 2001).

patches.theoryRelationship: Definition checked in the authors’ arXiv manuscript; the A/B partial-transpose convention conversion is explicit. Prior source links remain provenance.

assumptions: Phi is a Hermiticity-preserving linear map between finite-dimensional operator spaces, in particular a difference of two channels with common input/output spaces.
rho ranges over normalized density operators on input A tensor reference R, with dim(R)=dim(A); I is the identity superoperator on R.
variables: ||X||_1: trace norm; Phi: channel difference (not itself generally a channel); rho: joint input-reference state.
patches.regime: Source Theorem 3.51 gives a maximum over pure joint states. Convexity of the trace norm bounds every mixed-state value by a convex combination of pure-state values; pure states are included, proving equality with the displayed density-state supremum. The unrestricted-map diamond norm is NOT generally given by this state-only expression. No factor of 1/2 is included.

sourceLocations.locator: Theorem 3.51, Eq. (3.291), printed p. 176 / PDF p. 184; Definition 3.43, Eq. (3.256), printed p. 170 / PDF p. 178, completely bounded trace norm notation.
